 Search "Good Partner" Season 2 Premieres November 20: Cast, Storyline & Where to Watch
 Disha Paul 9 minutes ago 3 min read Jang Na-ra (left) and Kim Hye-yoon lead Good Partner Season 2, returning in November 20 with new legal battles, rivalries, and a fresh partnership. (SBS) Divorce cases, courtroom arguments, and lawyers who know exactly how to win a battle. Good Partner  is returning for another season, but this time Cha Eun-kyung will have a new partner by her side. 
 Starring Jang Nara and Kim Hye-yoon , Good Partner 2  is one of the upcoming Korean legal dramas to watch out for this November. The first season became a major hit, reaching a nationwide viewership rating of 17.7%. Now, the sequel promises more complicated divorce cases, new professional rivalries, and a fresh partnership. 
 So, when does Good Partner Season 2  premiere, and what can viewers expect? 
 When Does Good Partner Season 2 Release? 
 Good Partner Season 2  will premiere on November 20, 2026, at 9:50 p.m. KST  on SBS. 
 The drama will follow a Friday-Saturday broadcast schedule, with 16 episodes planned. Viewers can expect two episodes every week, subject to any changes in the broadcast schedule. 
 The new season arrives after a two-year gap, following the conclusion of the original series in September 2024. 
 Good Partner 2  (SBS) What Is Good Partner Season 2 About? 
 This time, Cha Eun-kyung ( Jang Nara ) is starting a new chapter as the managing partner of her own divorce-specialist law firm, Libom. 
 Good Partner 2 (SBS) Building a law firm from the ground up is not exactly an easy task, especially when complicated divorce cases keep arriving. To strengthen her team, Eun-kyung joins forces with Kang Hye-seong ( Kim Hye-yoon ), a fifth-year lawyer with a very different personality and approach to her work. 
 Eun-kyung brings experience and a practical understanding of divorce cases, while Hye-seong approaches her work with determination and passion. Their contrasting styles could lead to plenty of courtroom disagreements before they learn to become a proper team. 
 And they won't have an easy time outside their own office either. Park Tae-su ( Park Hae-jin ), the head of another law firm, is expected to become a major professional rival for Eun-kyung. 
 Who Is Returning for Good Partner Season 2? 
 Jang Nara returns as Cha Eun-kyung, while P.O reprises his role as Jeon Eun-ho. Kim Hye-yoon joins the main cast as Kang Hye-seong, and Park Hae-jin plays the new rival lawyer Park Tae-su. 
 One noticeable change is the absence of Nam Ji-hyun's Han Yu-ri, Eun-kyung's partner from the first season. Instead, Kim Hye-yoon's character will bring a new dynamic to the story. 
 The production team has also brought back writer Choi Yu-na, who is a practicing divorce lawyer, while Seo Min-jeong takes over directing duties. 
 Where to Watch Good Partner Season 2 
 The drama will first air on SBS in South Korea, with its premiere scheduled for November 20 at 9:50 p.m. KST . 
 For international viewers, Good Partner 2  is listed for streaming on Rakuten Viki, although availability may vary by country. Netflix's announced availability is limited to South Korea, so viewers elsewhere should check their local streaming catalogs before the premiere. 
 What Makes Season 2 Worth Watching? 
 The biggest attraction is the new partnership between Jang Nara and Kim Hye-yoon. Their characters have different personalities, legal strategies, and ideas about handling divorce cases, which should make their courtroom interactions particularly entertaining. 
 The show is also returning to one of its strongest elements: stories about relationships that don't always have simple answers. Not every divorce case is about catching a cheating spouse, and the consequences often affect entire families. 
 With a new law firm, fresh rivalries, and more complicated cases, Good Partner 2  has plenty of room to build on what made the first season successful. 
 Are you excited to see Jang Nara and Kim Hye-yoon become the new legal duo, or will you miss the original partnership with Nam Ji-hyun?
